docs.title: Copula
docs.text:
Copula lets reruns, edits and comparisons of an agent program share model samples, while each run on its own still sees what it would have seen without Copula: fresh, independent draws.

Run an unmodified program under copula run. The calls that an edited program makes exactly as before are read from earlier runs. The calls that changed are generated. Repeats that are meant to be independent, such as an unchanged rerun, another seed or another replicate, draw new samples.

$ copula run --exp demo -- python agent.py          # after editing one prompt
...
copula: run r-5e77ae7d7cf040a3 done: 6 calls: 3 reused, 3 generated, 0 joined
copula:   3 generated: new request -- closest earlier request (run r-74437c2a66b94f2e): messages[0] (system): '...eply OK, or give a corrected answer.' -> '...eply OK, or explain the mistake.'

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
Developing an agent means running it again and again with small changes, and every run pays for every model call, although most of them are the calls of the previous run. A response cache saves that cost but changes the statistics: it returns one stored response for every repeat of a request, inside a run, across seeds and across reruns. Repeated evaluations stop being independent, and the spread you measure between them shrinks to zero.

Copula numbers the repeats instead. Runs that share samples are in one group, and within a group the k-th identical request of a run reads the group's k-th sample. A run never reads one sample twice, so its own repeats stay independent. Which runs share a group follows from what you are doing: two versions of a program share, while an unchanged rerun or a replicate takes a group of its own.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• No changes to the program. OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages clients work through their base-URL variables, streaming and tool calls included. DSPy and GEPA programs get adapters automatically.
  • You pay for what changed. An edit regenerates only the calls whose requests changed, and everything downstream of them.
  • Sound by construction. Each run alone sees samples distributed as without Copula. The conditions are stated in Guarantees and limits.
  • Every generated call has a reason. The run summary and copula explain say why a call was not reused: what changed in the request, or which coordinate kept it apart.
  • Many runs at once. One copula server per project serves concurrent runs, Slurm arrays and launchers on other hosts. When two runs need the same sample at the same moment, it is generated once.
  • Standard library only. Python 3.9 or newer on Linux or macOS; vLLM, SGLang or any OpenAI-compatible API as the model server.

docs.title: When not to use it
docs.text:
• You want an exact replay of an earlier run. Copula gives an unchanged rerun new samples on purpose. Record-and-replay tools such as vcr.py replay exactly; Copula's own replay is not in this version.
  • What your program does depends on what is already stored, for example a program that skips work it finds in the store. The guarantee assumes it does not.
  • Your calls rely on provider-side state, such as server-side tools (web search) or conversations stored by the provider. Copula refuses such requests in this version.

docs.title: Comparison with other tools
docs.text:
Several kinds of tools store model responses. They differ in what a repeated request gets back, and so in what they are good for.

a repeat of a request gets suits Response caches the one stored response saving cost when repeats need not be independent Record and replay the recorded response, in recorded order exact, offline tests Occurrence-numbered caches the k-th stored response for the k-th repeat sharing without collapsing repeats Durable execution the result of the same step of the same execution resuming one execution after a failure Copula the k-th sample of its group, the group decided by the run edits, comparisons and replicates of one program

docs.title: Response caches
docs.text:
Framework caches (DSPy's, LangChain's set_llm_cache, AdalFlow's, AG2's) and gateway caches when they are turned on (LiteLLM, Portkey, OpenRouter) keep one response per request key. Unless the program puts something into the key that tells repeats apart, every repeat of a request gets that response: the five samples of a five-sample evaluation, and an unchanged rerun meant to measure variability, all see one response. Some caches offer such a key: DSPy's rollout_id (set by some modules, not by its evaluators and optimizers), AG2's cache_seed (one cache per seed value). Helicone's cache buckets keep several responses per key and return one of them at random, so repeats can still coincide.

Copula keeps the saving on calls that an edit did not change, but numbers repeats, so a run's repeats and its replicates stay independent. Turn framework caches off under Copula (the DSPy adapter does it for DSPy).

docs.title: Record and replay
docs.text:
vcr.py, pytest-recording and similar tools record the HTTP traffic of a test once and replay it afterwards, in order, offline. A changed request is a miss: it fails or goes to the network, depending on the record mode. They are the right tool for exact regression tests.

Copula does not replay an unchanged program: an unchanged rerun draws new samples. It shares between different versions instead, so an edit pays for what changed and is compared with its predecessor on the same samples.

docs.title: Occurrence-numbered caches
docs.text:
Cache Saver and Mnimi number identical requests within a namespace, so that the k-th repeat reads the k-th stored sample and other namespaces reuse the same list. This is the rule Copula's store uses, and the credit for it is theirs. DataDreamer (a seed per repeat) and Inspect (a cache per epoch) number repeats in more specific forms.

What Copula adds around the rule:

  • Which runs share is decided for you: groups follow from experiments, versions, slots and coordinate classes, so edits share, reruns and replicates do not, and the holdout phase is kept apart.
  • One store for every process of a project, safe under concurrency and crashes: identical samples needed at the same time are generated once, and a sample is written only complete.
  • Unmodified programs, through the base-URL variables, with read tracing for versions and adapters for DSPy and GEPA.
  • An explanation for every generated call.

docs.title: Durable execution
docs.text: Temporal, DBOS and Restate record the results of the steps of one execution, so that the execution can resume after a failure without repeating its side effects. They replay within one execution. Copula shares samples across executions, between versions of a program, and keeps reruns and replicates independent.

docs.title: What is guaranteed
docs.text:
Each run alone sees what it would see without Copula

Every run, on its own, sees samples distributed as they would be without Copula: its i-th repeat of a request is a fresh draw that it has not seen before.

This holds under three conditions:

  • (P) What the program does, and which cases it runs, does not depend on what is already in the store.
  • (C1) No run reads one sample address twice.
  • (C2) The next address a run asks for never depends on a sample it has not read.

Copula enforces C1 and C2: occurrences are numbered per run, a run that ended cannot send more requests, and a client retry re-reads only an occurrence whose response it never received. Condition P is yours: a program that, say, skips cases it finds already answered breaks it.

What sharing changes is the joint behaviour of several runs: two versions that read the same samples are correlated. That is the point. Their difference has less noise than the difference of two independent runs, and it costs less.

docs.title: What to keep in mind when you analyse results
docs.text:
Selecting on shared samples is optimistic

A version chosen because it scored best on some samples will score lower on new ones. Report final numbers from the holdout phase, whose sampled calls no search run has read.

Versions that share are not independent replicates

The scores of five versions that share samples are correlated, so their spread is not the spread of five independent runs. Estimate variability from replicates (seeds, reruns), which never share.

docs.title: Where outputs can differ from native runs
docs.text:
• Identical units in another order. Units with equal coordinates are numbered in the order they start. If that order changes between runs, they swap samples: each still sees a fresh draw, but the assignment is not a byte-exact repeat. A coordinate that tells them apart (case=...) makes it stable (arrival_order).
  • Seeded repeats inside a run. On a server that honours seeds, two identical seeded requests in one run usually return the same text natively; under Copula they are two samples of the seed's stream (Seeds).
  • Sampling defaults. Copula sends every sampling parameter explicitly. On vLLM and SGLang the values come from the model's generation_config.json when Copula finds the model files, as vLLM does natively; otherwise they are neutral, and a note says so (Connect a model server).
  • max_tokens. Requests that set none get --max-tokens (1024).
  • Text parts and roles. A content list of text parts is sent as one string, its parts joined by newlines; developer messages are sent as system.
  • Streaming. Streams are buffered: the content is the same, but it arrives at the end.
  • Unknown file contents count as unchanged. A run whose earlier run's files cannot be read counts as a rerun and gets new samples. Files over 256 MB are compared by size and modification time.
  • Reverted edits and runs after a failure count as reruns and get new samples (Versions).

docs.title: Limits of this version
docs.text:
• Requests: text content only (no images, audio or files); no request field Copula does not know (logprobs, logit_bias, best_of, reasoning_effort, vLLM's min_tokens or guided_json, ...); no requests that rely on provider-side state or server-side tools; no embeddings or legacy text completions (Refused fields).
  • Model servers: OpenAI-compatible ones (vLLM, SGLang, hosted APIs with an OpenAI-compatible endpoint). Anthropic clients work against them, but Anthropic's own API is not an upstream yet.
  • Tools: tool calls in model requests are served; the tools themselves run in the program and are not cached. There is no MCP proxy yet.
  • Adapters: DSPy and GEPA. Other frameworks run unchanged but as whole process runs, unless they mark units with copula.run or headers.
  • No replay or resume command, and copula.attach() works only under copula run.
  • Other caches: a framework cache that answers repeats from one stored sample hides those repeats from Copula. The DSPy adapter turns DSPy's off; turn off others (LangChain's set_llm_cache, LiteLLM caching, AG2's cache_seed, ...) yourself.
  • Calls that bypass the base URL (a client with a hard-coded endpoint) are not served.
  • Threads: unit context follows ThreadPoolExecutor workers and asyncio tasks; a thread started directly with threading.Thread carries no unit, so its calls belong to the process run.
  • Holdout runs: case disjointness from the search phase is checked for units only.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• .copula/ is private to its owner: it holds the secret behind run tokens, every prompt and every sample.
  • The endpoint listens on 127.0.0.1 by default. With --listen 0.0.0.0:PORT it serves other hosts over plain HTTP, guarded by per-run tokens and the server token: use it on a trusted network only.
  • Copula never forwards a program's key to the model server, and never hands the server's key to a program. copula run does not remove keys the program's environment already had.
  • Stored Responses objects are served to any valid run token of the project (GET /v1/responses/ID).

docs.title: When not to use Copula
docs.text:
• You need an exact replay of an earlier run, for a regression test that compares outputs byte for byte. Use a record-and-replay tool (Comparison).
  • Your program's behaviour depends on what is stored (condition P).
  • Your calls rely on provider-side state (server-side tools, provider-side conversations): Copula refuses them in this version.

docs.title: How Copula works
docs.text:
copula run ── registers the run ──▶ ┌──────────────── Copula server ───────────────┐
     │                               │ registry   runs, versions, slots, groups      │
     ▼                               │ store      samples, by address                │──▶ model server
 your program ── HTTP requests ────▶ │ call log   every answered call, and why       │    (vLLM, SGLang,
 (unchanged)  ◀── responses ──────── └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘     an API)

The program talks to Copula as if it were the model server. Copula decides, for each request, which stored sample answers it, or generates a new one and stores it.

docs.title: The life of one call
docs.text:
1. The run is registered. copula run tells the server the experiment, the coordinates of the run and the content digests of the files that decided earlier versions. The server answers with the run's version, slot and group, and a URL with a token that names the run.
  2. A request arrives on the run's URL. Headers may name a unit inside the run (an evaluation of one candidate on one case); a unit has a group of its own.
  3. Copula classifies the call from the request: a sampled call (cached per group), a greedy call (cached once for all runs, when the model's identity is established) or an uncached call (a role routed fresh). A request Copula cannot serve faithfully, such as one that relies on provider-side state, is refused.
  4. The call gets an address. For a sampled call it is the group, the model revision, the request after canonicalisation, and the occurrence: this is the k-th time the run sends this request in this group.
  5. The address is looked up. A stored sample is returned (reused). If another run is generating that very sample, the call waits for it (joined). Otherwise the sample is generated upstream, stored, and returned (generated).
  6. The call is logged, with its group, request digest and outcome, so that copula explain can later say why it was generated.
  7. The run ends. The launcher sends the set of project files the program read; their content decides whether the next run is a new version or an unchanged rerun.

docs.title: Occurrences: repeats stay independent
docs.text: Within a group, the k-th identical request of a run reads the group's k-th sample. A run that asks the same question three times gets samples 1, 2 and 3, three independent draws, as it would without Copula. A later version of the program that asks it five times reads samples 1 to 3 and generates 4 and 5. A run never reads one sample twice, and it never reads a sample it did not ask for.

docs.title: Versions and slots: who shares
docs.text:
A group is a pool of samples. Which runs share a group is decided by the registry:

  • A run whose program or files changed since every earlier run of the experiment, or whose compare coordinates differ, is a new version. It takes the smallest slot its version has not used, which is slot 1, and slot 1 of every version of an experiment (with equal replicate and case values) is one group. So all versions share.
  • A run whose program and files are unchanged since an earlier run is a rerun of that version. It takes the next slot (2, 3, ...), and a new slot is a new group. So reruns get new samples.
  • Runs that differ in a replicate or case coordinate, in the phase or in the experiment are in different groups whatever their slot.

The quickstart's runs, side by side:

run what changed version slot group shares with 1 first run v1 1 A 2 the check prompt v2 1 A run 1, on the calls the edit did not change 3 nothing v2 2 B nobody: a rerun is a new replicate --set seed=1 a replicate coordinate v2 1 C other runs with seed 1

docs.title: Greedy calls
docs.text: A call with temperature 0 (or top_k 1) has one answer per model, so it does not need numbering. When the model's identity is established (the files it loaded are known), Copula caches greedy calls once for every run, whatever its experiment, phase or group, and repeats read that one answer, as they would natively. Without an established identity, greedy calls are treated like sampled ones, per group (When two calls are the same).

docs.title: Concurrency and failures
docs.text:
• One server holds the store and serves every run of the project; identical samples that are needed at the same moment are generated once.
  • Transport failures and an overloaded or misconfigured upstream are retried and never stored; an error the request itself causes (a prompt that is too long) is stored as that sample's result, as the model server would give it every time. A sample is written only complete.
  • A client retry (the openai SDK's x-stainless-retry-count, or an Idempotency-Key) of a request whose response was lost reads the same occurrence again instead of taking the next one, so client retries do not consume samples.
  • A run that ended cannot send more requests: a late attempt would re-read samples its client already received.

docs.title: Terms
docs.text:
term meaning run one launched command (a process run), or a unit inside it unit a run inside a process run, with coordinates of its own: one evaluation of one candidate on one case, say experiment the runs that may share samples (--exp NAME) version the program as it was: its compare coordinates and the content of the files it read slot the number of a run among the runs of its version with the same replicate and case values: 1 for the first, 2 for its first rerun, ... group a pool of samples; runs in one group share occurrence for a request, the number of times the run has sent it in its group so far; the k-th occurrence reads sample k (x-copula-rank) ordinal for a unit, the number of units with the same coordinates the process has opened so far address what identifies a stored sample (When two calls are the same) phase search or holdout; their sampled calls never share

copula explain names the model a call went to and its class: actor:s is a sampled call to the default model (actor), actor:d a greedy one, actor:u an uncached one; other served models are m1, m2, ...

docs.title: Where the ideas come from
docs.text: Numbering identical requests so that the k-th repeat reads the k-th stored sample is the rule of Cache Saver and Mnimi. Copula adds the run structure around it: which runs share a group, decided from versions, slots and coordinates; one concurrent, crash-safe store for every process of a project; and explanations of every miss.

docs.title: When two calls are the same
docs.text: Two calls can share a sample only if they have the same address. This page lists everything that goes into it, and what does not.

docs.title: The address of a call
docs.text:
call address sampled (the default) group, model revision, request, occurrence greedy, model identity established model revision, request uncached none: drawn anew every time
  • Group: decided by the run, its coordinates and slot (Runs, coordinates and versions), a role's route, and the request's seed.
  • Model revision: the served model, the model server's kind and version, the sampling table, serving settings (--identity-extra), and the model's files when Copula can read them: config, tokenizer and every weight file (Connect a model server).
  • Request: the request after canonicalisation (below).
  • Occurrence: for the k-th identical request of a run in its group, k. A request with n=3 takes three consecutive occurrences.

docs.title: The request
docs.text:
The request in the address is the chat request after canonicalisation:

  • Messages, including tool calls and tool results. Content sent as a list of text parts is the texts joined by newlines (as vLLM joins them), so it is the same request as that string, and the role developer is read as system. Content parts other than text (images, audio, files) are refused in this version.
  • Every sampling parameter: temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, repetition_penalty, stop, chat_template_kwargs. Parameters the client left out are filled from the model's pinned sampling table, so a request that states a default and one that leaves it out are the same request.
  • max_tokens (or max_completion_tokens), set to --max-tokens when the client sets none.
  • tools, tool_choice, response_format and parallel_tool_calls when they are set.

Not part of the request, because they do not change the sample: stream and stream_options; user, metadata, store, service_tier, prompt_cache_key, safety_identifier and timeout; client headers. n and seed are not part of it either, but they decide the occurrences and the group.

A change anywhere in the request makes it a new request, including a change you did not mean: a timestamp in the system prompt, a random id, the iteration order of a set. copula explain shows the first difference (new_request).

docs.title: How a call is classified
docs.text:
Copula infers how to treat a call from the request, as the table says. The first matching row applies.

the request treated as refers to provider-side state: previous_response_id of a response Copula did not issue, conversation, thread_id refused: HTTP 400 (404 for an unknown previous_response_id in the Responses API) uses a server-side tool (a tool whose type is not function, such as web search) refused: HTTP 400 comes with a role routed fresh uncached sets a seed sampled, in the seed's own stream temperature 0 or top_k 1, and the model's identity is established greedy: one answer for all runs, across groups, phases and experiments temperature 0 or top_k 1, identity not established sampled, per group (W12) anything else sampled

Greedy decoding on an inference server is close to, but not exactly, deterministic, so Copula treats a greedy call as deterministic only when it knows exactly which model answers it. A Responses request whose previous_response_id names a response Copula issued is expanded into the full conversation and treated like any other request.

docs.title: Seeds
docs.text:
A seed in the request body selects a sample stream: the group of a seeded request is derived from the run's group and the seed. Requests with seed=7 share samples with other seed=7 requests of the group, and the k-th identical seeded request of a run reads the k-th sample of the seed's stream. A request with seed=7 and n=3 uses the streams 7, 8 and 9.

Copula does not send the client's seed to the model server. For vLLM it sends an engine seed of its own, derived from the sample's address, so the draw does not depend on the client's seed value but each seed still gets its own samples.

One difference from native behaviour: on a server that honours seeds, two identical seeded requests inside one run usually return the same text natively. Under Copula they are two occurrences, so they get two samples of the seed's stream. A note in the run summary says so.

docs.title: Refused fields
docs.text:
A request is refused with HTTP 400 (invalid_call) when it carries a field Copula does not know: anything besides the messages, the sampling parameters, max_tokens/max_completion_tokens, tools, tool_choice, response_format, parallel_tool_calls, n, seed, stream, stream_options and the ignored fields above. This holds inside extra_body too. Refused, among others:

  • logprobs, top_logprobs, logit_bias, best_of, reasoning_effort, prediction, modalities, audio, web_search_options, functions and function_call;
  • server-specific parameters such as vLLM's min_tokens, ignore_eos, guided_json or skip_special_tokens.

Copula either cannot store what they ask for, or cannot be sure that two requests that differ in them are different requests. A field that Copula does not understand is never silently dropped.

docs.title: Runs and units
docs.text:
A run is one launched command: copula run -- COMMAND registers a process run. Inside it, units are smaller runs, each with coordinates of its own, typically one evaluation of one candidate on one case. Units come from:

  • framework adapters (DSPy module calls, Prompt and harness optimizers);
  • with copula.run(candidate=..., case=...): in Python (Python API);
  • X-Copula-Coords headers on requests, from any language (HTTP interface).

A unit's coordinates are merged over its process run's. The k-th unit with the same coordinates in one process is a different unit from the first (ordinal k), so it reads new samples, like a repeated request.

docs.title: Coordinates
docs.text:
Coordinates are names and values that describe a run:

  • The command line. Every --name value, --name=value, -o value and Hydra-style name=value (also +name=value) of the command's arguments; a lone -- ends the options. Positional words give none. A flag followed by a word that is not an option takes that word as its value, so python -u agent.py gives u=agent.py and --verbose data.csv gives verbose=data.csv: harmless replicates while the command line stays the same. sh -c SCRIPT gives the coordinate c, the whole script, so put the program directly after -- when its arguments matter.
  • --set name=value, for coordinates the command line does not carry.
  • SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID, as slurm_array_task_id.
  • Adapters, such as candidate, case and optimizer_seed of the DSPy adapter.

Names are compared in lower case, without leading dashes and with - read as _: --Output-Dir is output_dir. Values are strings, so --seed 0 and a run that sets no seed differ.

docs.title: Classes
docs.text:
The class of a name decides what it does to sharing:

class meaning effect compare what you compare: variants, configs, candidates, budgets left out of the group: runs that differ in it share; it makes a run a new version replicate an index of independent repeats: seeds, trials part of the group: runs that differ in it never share case the input part of the group: runs that differ in it never share annotation output and log paths, run names recorded only

Every name that is not built in is a replicate (log_level and verbosity too): an unknown name can only cost samples, never make two runs share that should not. Note that version is a built-in compare coordinate, unrelated to the versions Copula derives from files. The built-in names, and the names each --recipe adds, are in Coordinate names and recipes. --compare, --replicate, --case and --annotation override the class of a name for one run.

docs.title: Phases
docs.text: A run is in the search phase unless --phase holdout (or copula.holdout(), or an adapter) puts it in the holdout phase, which has groups of its own: the sampled calls of the two phases never share. (Greedy calls to a model with an established identity are global, in every phase.) A holdout unit whose case the search phase of the experiment already used is refused with HTTP 409 (W5a); for whole process runs in the holdout phase the cases are not checked. Report final numbers from the holdout phase: a version selected on shared search samples is scored there on samples the search never saw.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
With --exp, every process run records the project files it read and their content (Run an existing program). A new run is an unchanged rerun of the most recent earlier run of the experiment that has the same compare values and whose files all still have the content they had. Otherwise it is a new version.

When Copula cannot know, it counts the files as unchanged, so the run is a rerun and draws new samples, the safe direction:

  • an earlier run is still running, so its read set is not known yet;
  • an earlier run failed (non-zero exit), so its read set was not recorded, and no successful run with the same compare values came after it;
  • an earlier run read no project file at all;
  • a file cannot be read now (deleted, or not visible on this host).

Files larger than 256 MB are compared by size and modification time instead of content.

Three consequences are worth knowing:

  • Reverting an edit makes the program equal to an earlier version again, so the run is a rerun of that version and draws new samples.
  • After a failed run, the next run is counted as a rerun of the failed one (its files are unknown), so it shares nothing with earlier versions. Once a run succeeds, the following runs are matched against it again.
  • A program Copula does not trace records no reads, so every later run counts as unchanged; name its files with --track (Run an existing program).

docs.title: Groups and slots
docs.text:
For a process run, with H a hash and the counter the key under which slots are numbered:

counter = H(experiment, phase, granularity, replicate values, case values, version)
slot    = the smallest slot not yet used under that counter
group   = H(experiment, phase, granularity, replicate values, case values, slot)

The granularity is process or unit. Units use the same rule, with the unit's version derived from its process run's version and its own compare values. The version is in the counter but not in the group: every new version takes slot 1 of its counter, and slot 1 is one group for all versions. An unchanged rerun finds slot 1 used and takes slot 2: a new group. Matching the version and claiming the slot happen in one transaction, so two runs launched at the same moment never take the same slot.

A run outside any experiment (no --exp) gets a fresh group of its own.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Inside copula.decision(), a unit reads the slot of the decision's first unit on the same case, unless this unit's counter has already used that slot; then it takes its own next slot. A parent and a child compared in one decision then read the same samples where their calls agree. The GEPA adapter opens one decision per proposal.

docs.title: Roles and routes
docs.text: A call made with a role (copula.role(name) or X-Copula-Role) is placed by the run's routes: --route ROLE=run (the default: the run's group), global (one group per experiment, phase and role), per:COORD (one group per value of a coordinate) or fresh (uncached). Routes need an experiment; without --exp they are ignored. Routes let, say, the proposer of an optimizer share across runs of one seed while evaluations stay per run.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Copula needs Python 3.9 or newer on Linux and nothing else: it uses only the standard library (macOS is not tested). Read tracing of Node programs needs Node 18.19 or newer.

Copula is not on PyPI yet. Install it from a checkout of the repository:

git clone https://github.com/Bowen-Sun-0728/Copula.git
pip install ./Copula

The extras install the clients that the tests and examples use: pip install './Copula[openai]', [anthropic] or [dspy]. Copula does not need them itself.

Check the installation:

$ copula --version
copula 0.1.0.dev0

python -m copula is the same command, for environments where the copula script is not on PATH.

docs.title: What gets installed
docs.text:
• The copula command: run, server, explain and ls (Command line).
  • The copula Python package. import copula needs nothing beyond the standard library, and programs need it only to describe their structure in more detail than Copula infers (Python API).
  • copula.kernel, the sample store and the cache manager underneath.

Copula keeps its state in a .copula/ directory in the project, created on the first run (Files and environment).

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This page takes about five minutes and needs no GPU and no API key: Copula's mock model stands in for a model server until the last step. You need Copula (Install) and the openai package (pip install openai).

docs.title: 1. A small agent
docs.text:
The agent answers three questions, then asks the model to check each answer. It is an ordinary OpenAI client program: nothing in it knows about Copula.

agent.py
from openai import OpenAI

ANSWER = "Answer the question in one sentence."
CHECK = "Check the answer. Reply OK, or give a corrected answer."
QUESTIONS = ["Why is the sky blue?", "What is a prime number?", "Who wrote Hamlet?"]

client = OpenAI()  # OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY come from the environment


def ask(system, user):
    r = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct",
        messages=[{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}],
        temperature=0.7,
    )
    return r.choices[0].message.content


for q in QUESTIONS:
    answer = ask(ANSWER, q)
    verdict = ask(CHECK, f"Q: {q}\nA: {answer}")
    print(f"{answer}  {verdict}")

docs.title: 2. Run it under Copula
docs.text:
copula run starts the program with its model endpoint pointed at Copula. --exp demo names the experiment: runs of one experiment can share samples. --mock serves Copula's mock model, whose reply is a token that is unique to each sample.

$ copula run --exp demo --mock -- python agent.py
copula: run r-64bcd82a96ad410d  exp=demo  dev: version v-1b298059bbfc4108, slot 1  group g-0e5d5aee9cfa7a183956942b
copula: served by embedded server (mock model)
copula: new version (compared with earlier versions of demo)
copula: attach: attached to http://127.0.0.1:41219/ (threads copy context; headers on httpx, httpx2, http.client)
mock:a2ea4ab3b827641bb0f6e35c  mock:b9bd584e3aa940edbfb3c232
mock:931a3f9b9ced931fd91106e0  mock:ab3a1fec6eefb886b044a396
mock:08a4c8313a48b2234005563d  mock:28d7ed1f7420908c9fc192db
copula: run r-64bcd82a96ad410d done: 6 calls: 0 reused, 6 generated, 0 joined
copula:   6 generated: new request -- no earlier run of the experiment called this model
copula:   details: copula explain r-64bcd82a96ad410d

The program printed an answer and a verdict per question. The first line says how Copula placed the run: a new version of the experiment (there was none before), slot 1, and the group whose samples it reads and writes. The last lines are the summary: all six calls were generated, because no earlier run had made them.

docs.title: 3. Edit a prompt and run again
docs.text:
Change the check prompt, the way you would while developing:

CHECK = "Check the answer. Reply OK, or explain the mistake."

$ copula run --exp demo --mock -- python agent.py
copula: run r-fe7557a3a3f54eff  exp=demo  dev: version v-52dffde4430a45d5, slot 1  group g-0e5d5aee9cfa7a183956942b
copula: served by embedded server (mock model)
copula: new version (compared with earlier versions of demo)
copula: attach: attached to http://127.0.0.1:33231/ (threads copy context; headers on httpx, httpx2, http.client)
mock:a2ea4ab3b827641bb0f6e35c  mock:c484e3cf1ad4ee562ac3fc19
mock:931a3f9b9ced931fd91106e0  mock:0e4ae7fc82d80e7d6edda1d6
mock:08a4c8313a48b2234005563d  mock:11889e9f5bf2ca419c960fd0
copula: run r-fe7557a3a3f54eff done: 6 calls: 3 reused, 3 generated, 0 joined
copula:   3 generated: new request -- closest earlier request (run r-64bcd82a96ad410d): messages[0] (system): '...eply OK, or give a corrected answer.' -> '...eply OK, or explain the mistake.'
copula:   details: copula explain r-fe7557a3a3f54eff

Three calls were reused and three generated. The answers (the first column) are the ones of the first run: the edited program made those calls exactly as before, so they were read from the store. The checks changed, so they were generated, and the summary shows what changed in the request.

This is the point of Copula. The two versions are compared on the same answers, so the comparison is paired and less noisy, and the second run paid only for the calls the edit changed.

docs.title: 4. Run it again without changes
docs.text:
$ copula run --exp demo --mock -- python agent.py
copula: run r-0d453dd20c9e4bb8  exp=demo  dev: version v-52dffde4430a45d5, slot 2  group g-99de249e733e13798f798660
copula: served by embedded server (mock model)
copula: unchanged since run r-fe7557a3a3f54eff: a rerun (new slot, new samples)
copula: attach: attached to http://127.0.0.1:37947/ (threads copy context; headers on httpx, httpx2, http.client)
mock:6bec6bcd45de1d933642e841  mock:c5eb9ea273c29ccff825b5fd
mock:3d2c61f3e177f99dcdcf6c63  mock:942f9f67d753c68356accaea
mock:f1fc0cb4b70c95b5bb328299  mock:c2cf7782fdfdc47ff0b753d4
copula: run r-0d453dd20c9e4bb8 done: 6 calls: 0 reused, 6 generated, 0 joined
copula:   3 generated: unchanged rerun (new slot) -- the program is unchanged since run r-fe7557a3a3f54eff, so this run is a rerun: it takes a new slot (2; that run: 1) and draws new samples by design
copula:   3 generated: new request -- closest earlier request (run r-fe7557a3a3f54eff): messages[1] (user): '...ue?\nA: mock:a2ea4ab3b827641bb0f6e35c' -> '...ue?\nA: mock:6bec6bcd45de1d933642e841'
copula:   details: copula explain r-0d453dd20c9e4bb8

Nothing was reused. The program and the files it read are unchanged, so this run is a rerun, and a rerun is a new replicate: it takes a new slot and draws new samples. Copula never gives a rerun the sampled outputs of the run it repeats, because a rerun is how you measure how much the outputs vary. The answers are new, so the checks of those answers are new requests too.

docs.title: 5. Ask why
docs.text:
copula explain shows how the latest run was placed and why its calls were generated:

$ copula explain
run r-0d453dd20c9e4bb8  experiment demo  phase search  status done
  dev: version v-52dffde4430a45d5, slot 2; group g-99de249e733e13798f798660; rerun of r-fe7557a3a3f54eff
  files read: 1; units: 0
  calls: 6: 0 reused, 6 generated, 0 joined, 0 errors
      3 generated: unchanged rerun (new slot)
          e.g. the program is unchanged since run r-fe7557a3a3f54eff, so this run is a rerun: it takes a new slot (2; that run: 1) and draws new samples by design
      3 generated: new request
          e.g. closest earlier request (run r-fe7557a3a3f54eff): messages[1] (user): '...ue?\nA: mock:a2ea4ab3b827641bb0f6e35c' -> '...ue?\nA: mock:6bec6bcd45de1d933642e841'

copula ls lists the runs of the project:

$ copula ls
RUN                    EXPERIMENT   PHASE    KIND     STATUS   VERSION             SLOT  GROUP
r-64bcd82a96ad410d     demo         search   process  done     v-1b298059bbfc4108  1     g-0e5d5aee9cfa7a183956942b
r-fe7557a3a3f54eff     demo         search   process  done     v-52dffde4430a45d5  1     g-0e5d5aee9cfa7a183956942b
r-0d453dd20c9e4bb8     demo         search   process  done     v-52dffde4430a45d5  2     g-99de249e733e13798f798660

Versions 1 and 2 hold slot 1 of the same group, so they share; the rerun holds slot 2 of another group. Why was this call generated? explains every reason copula explain can give.

docs.title: 6. Use your own model server
docs.text:
Drop --mock. Copula then forwards to the server your program would have used, the one in OPENAI_BASE_URL:

$ vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct --port 8000 &
$ export OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000/v1
$ copula run --exp demo-qwen -- python agent.py

Samples are stored per model revision, so the mock model's samples are never served for Qwen. Connect a model server covers vLLM, SGLang and hosted APIs.

docs.title: Compare, repeat and sweep
docs.text:
Which runs share samples is decided by their coordinates: names and values Copula reads from the command line (--variant strict, seed=1), from --set k=v and from framework adapters. Each name has a class (Runs, coordinates and versions):

  • compare: what you are comparing (variant, prompt, config, candidate, ...). Runs that differ in it share samples.
  • replicate: an index of independent repeats (seed, trial, rep, ...). Runs that differ in it never share. Every name Copula does not know is a replicate, the safe direction.
  • case: the input (case, example, task_id, ...). Runs that differ in it never share.
  • annotation: recorded and ignored (output_dir, log_dir, run_name, ...).

--compare NAME, --replicate NAME, --case NAME and --annotation NAME set the class of a name; the built-in names are listed in Coordinate names and recipes.

The examples on this page use this agent:

agent.py
import argparse

from openai import OpenAI

CHECKS = {
    "short": "Check the answer. Reply OK, or give a corrected answer.",
    "strict": "Check every claim in the answer. Reply OK only if all are correct.",
}
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--variant", default="short", choices=CHECKS)
parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
args = parser.parse_args()
client = OpenAI()


def ask(system, user):
    r = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct", temperature=0.7,
        messages=[{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}])
    return r.choices[0].message.content


for q in ["Why is the sky blue?", "What is a prime number?", "Who wrote Hamlet?"]:
    answer = ask("Answer the question in one sentence.", q)
    verdict = ask(CHECKS[args.variant], f"Q: {q}\nA: {answer}")
    print(f"{answer}  {verdict}")

docs.title: Replicates
docs.text:
To measure how much the outputs vary, run replicates. seed is a replicate coordinate, so --seed 1 shares nothing with the runs above:

$ copula run --exp ab --mock -- python agent.py --variant strict --seed 1

copula: served by embedded server (mock model)

docs.title: Repeated calls inside a run
docs.text:
A run that sends the same request several times gets a new sample each time: the k-th identical request of a run reads the k-th sample of its group. Repeats inside a run are independent, as they are without Copula.

vote.py
import sys
from collections import Counter

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()
n = int(sys.argv[1].split("=")[1])            # n=3
votes = Counter()
for _ in range(n):
    r = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct", temperature=1.0,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Is 91 a prime? Answer yes or no."}])
    votes[r.choices[0].message.content] += 1
print(len(votes), "distinct answers")

Larger budgets read the samples of smaller ones when the budget is a compare coordinate. n is not a built-in name, so --compare n says that runs with different n are compared:

$ copula run --exp vote --mock --compare n -- python vote.py n=3

copula:   3 generated: new request -- no earlier run of the experiment called this model
copula:   details: copula explain r-9106ed4ed327492e

5 distinct answers

The run with n=5 read the three samples of the n=3 run and generated two more. Without --compare n, n would be a replicate and the two runs would share nothing. The tts recipe classes n, beam_width and num_beams as compare coordinates (recipes).

docs.title: Sweeps
docs.text:
A sweep over a parameter compares its values within each seed:

$ for lr in 1e-4 3e-4 1e-3; do
>   copula run --exp sweep --compare lr -- python train_agent.py --lr $lr --seed 1
> done

Unknown names are replicates, so without --compare lr every value of lr would be generated from scratch: correct, only more expensive. To run the sweep in parallel, start one server for the project first.

In a Slurm array, SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID becomes a replicate coordinate of every run on its own.

docs.title: Final numbers: the holdout phase
docs.text:
Runs that reuse samples are compared on the same draws, which is what you want while developing. A version chosen because it did well on some samples is optimistic when it is scored on those same samples. Score the final choice in the holdout phase, whose sampled calls share nothing with the search phase:

$ copula run --exp ab --phase holdout -- python agent.py --variant strict --split test

Inside one process, copula.holdout() does the same for a block of code (Prompt and harness optimizers).

docs.title: Seeds in requests
docs.text: A seed in the request body is a stream of its own: the requests with seed=7 share samples with other seed=7 requests of the group, and the k-th identical seeded request of a run reads the k-th sample of that stream. Copula does not send the client's seed to the model server (Seeds).

docs.title: Run an existing program
docs.text:
copula run starts a command as one run and serves its model calls:

copula run [--exp NAME] [options] -- COMMAND [ARGS...]

Everything after -- is the command, unchanged. copula run exits with the command's exit status (128 + N when signal N killed it). Ctrl-C in a terminal reaches the command directly; kill of the launcher (SIGTERM) is forwarded to it.

docs.title: What changes for the program
docs.text:
The command runs with its model endpoint pointed at Copula. These variables are set in its environment; the full list is in Files and environment.

variable value OPENAI_BASE_URL, OPENAI_API_BASE, LLM_BASE_URL, COPULA_URL the run's URL, http://127.0.0.1:PORT/r/TOKEN/v1 ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_API_BASE the same URL without /v1 (the Anthropic SDK adds it) OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY copula, if they are not set already COPULA_MODEL the default model of the model server PYTHONPATH Copula's start-up hook first: it records the files Python reads NODE_OPTIONS --require of Copula's read recorder (with --exp)

The token in the URL names the run, so any client that takes a base URL works without sending extra headers. Copula never forwards the key the program sends: it talks to the model server with its own (Connect a model server). The rest of the environment is left as it was, so a key that was already set is still visible to the program.

Clients tested with Copula: the openai and anthropic Python SDKs and DSPy 3 (through LiteLLM). Any other client that reads one of these variables works the same way. A program that hard-codes its base URL needs one change: take it from OPENAI_BASE_URL.

docs.title: Without an experiment
docs.text:
Without --exp the run is served, logged and explained, but it shares nothing with any other run. Here a shell script calls the endpoint with curl:

ask.sh
curl -s "$OPENAI_BASE_URL/chat/completions" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "m", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}' |
  python -c 'import json, sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["choices"][0]["message"]["content"])'

$ copula run --mock -- sh ask.sh
copula: run r-7b008e906a924526  exp=-  no experiment: fresh group (O1)  group g-ae4de1fb42574fb3bfd7
copula: served by embedded server (mock model)
mock:9e2429903d29e0a65fc0379f
copula: run r-7b008e906a924526 done: 1 calls: 0 reused, 1 generated, 0 joined
copula:   1 generated: new request -- no earlier run sent it
copula:   details: copula explain r-7b008e906a924526

With --exp NAME, runs of the experiment share: an edited program reads the samples of the calls it makes as before (Quickstart).

docs.title: Protocols
docs.text:
endpoint protocol POST /v1/chat/completions OpenAI Chat Completions: tools, response_format, n, seed, streaming POST /v1/responses, GET /v1/responses/ID OpenAI Responses, including previous_response_id chains of responses Copula issued POST /v1/messages Anthropic Messages, including tools and streaming GET /v1/models the models the server serves

Each protocol is translated into a chat request for the OpenAI-compatible model server, and the sample is rendered back in the protocol the client used. A streaming and a non-streaming request with the same content are the same request. Streams are buffered: the client receives keep-alives while the sample is generated, then the whole response as stream events.

What is refused with HTTP 400 in this version:

  • content parts other than text (images, audio, files);
  • requests that rely on provider-side state (previous_response_id of a response Copula did not issue, conversation, thread_id) or use server-side tools such as web search;
  • every request field Copula does not know, for example logprobs, logit_bias, best_of, reasoning_effort, or vLLM's min_tokens and guided_json, also inside extra_body.

Fields that do not change the output (user, metadata, store, service_tier, timeout, ...) are accepted and ignored (When two calls are the same).

docs.title: Versions: the files the program reads
docs.text:
With --exp, Copula decides whether a run is a new version of the program or an unchanged rerun from the content of the project files the program read (Runs, coordinates and versions).

  • Python children (every Python process the command starts, at any depth) are traced by an audit hook: files opened for reading and the source files of imported modules.
  • Node children are traced by a preloaded module (require, import and fs reads).
  • Other programs: name the files with --track GLOB (repeatable, relative to the project, ** allowed), for example --track 'prompts/**' --track config.yaml.

Only files under the project directory count (--project, by default the current directory). Files the run also wrote, .copula/, virtual environments (venv, .venv, env, site-packages), node_modules, caches and VCS directories are ignored, and so are build/ and dist/ for Node.

A program Copula cannot trace looks unchanged forever

If Copula records no file reads for a run, a later run finds nothing that changed and counts as an unchanged rerun: it draws new samples, and edits never share. This happens for programs that are neither Python nor Node (a compiled binary, a shell script that does the work itself), and for Python started with -I, -E or -S, which skip Copula's start-up hook. Name their files with --track. Python and Node programs started by a shell script are traced.

docs.title: Inside a Python program
docs.text:
With --exp, Python children are attached to their run (copula.attach()), which prints one line:

copula: attach: attached to http://127.0.0.1:35135/ (threads copy context; headers on httpx, httpx2, http.client)

Attaching copies Copula's context into worker threads and adds it to requests sent to Copula, so that copula.run(...) and the framework adapters can mark units (Python API). It changes nothing else in the program. COPULA_QUIET=1 silences the line; --no-attach turns attaching off.

docs.title: Other languages
docs.text: A program in any language can mark units itself by sending X-Copula-* headers with its requests (HTTP interface). Without them, the whole command is one run.

docs.title: Connect a model server
docs.text:
Copula sits between the program and an OpenAI-compatible model server, the upstream. By default the upstream is the server the program would have used: the OPENAI_BASE_URL of the copula run or copula server process. --upstream URL names another one.

$ export OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://gpu-node:8000/v1        # what the program used before
$ copula run --exp triage -- python agent.py

At start Copula asks the upstream for its models (GET /v1/models) and tells vLLM and SGLang, which it runs differently, from other OpenAI-compatible APIs. The banner says what it found:

copula: served by embedded server (vllm http://gpu-node:8000/v1, engine seed per address)
copula:   note: sampling defaults: Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct generation_config

Model options belong to whoever serves the run: copula run when it serves the run itself, or copula server for every run of the project (One server for many runs).

docs.title: vLLM and SGLang
docs.text:
Sampling defaults. A request that leaves a sampling parameter unset gets the server's default, and two requests that differ only in stating that default must get the same sample. So Copula sends every sampling parameter explicitly, from a pinned table:

  1. --defaults JSON or --defaults @FILE, if given, for the default model; it names all nine sampling parameters (temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, repetition_penalty, stop, chat_template_kwargs);
  2. otherwise the model's generation_config.json (temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, repetition_penalty), which is what vLLM applies by default, so the samples are those of the server used natively;
  3. otherwise neutral values (temperature 1, top_p 1, no top_k), with a note saying so.

Copula finds generation_config.json in --model-dir DIR, or in the directory the server reports for the model (when the server runs on this host), or in this host's Hugging Face cache for the model id. A LoRA adapter takes the table of its base model.

Model identity. Copula stores samples per model revision, so a sample of one checkpoint is never served for another. The revision covers the served model name, the server version, the sampling table and, when it can read them, the model's files: config.json, the tokenizer files and every weight file, so a re-saved or re-sharded checkpoint is a new revision. --identity-extra JSON adds serving settings that change outputs, such as dtype or quantisation.

The identity is established only from files the server itself loaded: --model-dir, or the local directory the server reports when it runs on this host. A Hugging Face id, or a server on another host, gives the sampling table from the local cache but no established identity, and a note says so:

copula:   note: identity of Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct not established (model files from a cache snapshot or another host): greedy calls are cached per group (W12); pass --model-dir to establish it

The identity matters for greedy calls (temperature 0 or top_k 1): with an established identity they are deterministic and cached once for every run; without one they are cached per group like any sampled call (When two calls are the same).

Engine seed. Copula sends vLLM a seed per sample, derived from the sample's address with a secret of the store (--engine-seed address, the default for vLLM under auto). A sample does not depend on the server's --seed, and the same address asks for the same draw again. SGLang gets no engine seed under auto; --engine-seed off turns it off for vLLM too. The seed a client puts in its request is never sent upstream (Seeds).

docs.title: Hosted and other OpenAI-compatible APIs
docs.text:
$ export OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1 OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
$ copula run --exp triage -- python agent.py
  • Key. Copula sends the key in its own OPENAI_API_KEY (or in the variable --api-key-env names). It never forwards a key sent by the program.
  • Parameters. temperature, top_p and the penalties are always sent, with OpenAI's defaults when the client sets none; pass --defaults for a provider whose defaults differ. top_k, min_p, repetition_penalty and chat_template_kwargs are sent only when they differ from neutral values. max_tokens becomes max_completion_tokens for models that require it.
  • Identity. An API model's weights are not visible, so its identity is never established: greedy calls are cached per group. There is no engine seed, and --identity-extra does not apply.

docs.title: Names, limits and failures
docs.text:
• Model names. Copula serves the names the upstream lists. --model NAME=SERVED adds a client-side name for a served model; --model '*' sends any unknown name to the default model; --served-model NAME picks the default model (it is also the only model when the upstream does not list its models).
  • max_tokens. Requests that set none get --max-tokens (1024), so the sample does not depend on a server-side limit.
  • Failures. Connection errors and timeouts, HTTP 5xx, 408, 409, 429 and misconfiguration (401, 403, 404, 405, 407) are retried with backoff (--max-attempts, --backoff) and never stored; when the attempts run out the client gets HTTP 502 and a later request tries again. Any other 4xx is caused by the request itself (a context that is too long, a malformed tool schema): it is stored as that sample's result, as the model server would answer it every time, and the client gets HTTP 400 model_error.
  • Timeouts and concurrency. --timeout (900 s per upstream request), --workers (64 upstream requests at once), --inflight (64 generations per model), --wait-ready S to wait for an upstream that is still starting.

docs.title: The mock model
docs.text:
--mock serves a model that needs no server: each reply is a token that is unique to the sample (mock:...). The token depends only on the sample's address, so an experiment gives the same tokens in every project (a run without --exp has a fresh group, and so fresh tokens). It accepts any model name unless --model lists names. Use it to try Copula, and to test a program's control flow.

--mock-script FILE.py:FUNC makes the replies depend on the request. The function receives the request body and the sample's token and returns text, a dict of sample fields (content, tool_calls, finish_reason), or None for the plain token:

replies.py
def reply(body, token):
    question = body["messages"][-1]["content"]
    if "capital" in question:
        return "Paris"            # the same text for every sample of this request
    return f"I am not sure ({token})"
ask_capital.py
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()
for q in ["What is the capital of France?", "What is love?"]:
    r = client.chat.completions.create(model="any", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": q}])
    print(r.choices[0].message.content)

$ copula run --mock --mock-script replies.py:reply -- python ask_capital.py
copula: run r-b4e2f7a08fe84b3a  exp=-  no experiment: fresh group (O1)  group g-fdecf26b0001459486e3
copula: served by embedded server (mock model)
Paris
I am not sure (mock:eddef53502ac7ab118187002)
copula: run r-b4e2f7a08fe84b3a done: 2 calls: 0 reused, 2 generated, 0 joined
copula:   2 generated: new request -- no earlier run sent it
copula:   details: copula explain r-b4e2f7a08fe84b3a

--mock-script implies --mock. --mock-nonce gives the mock other tokens, and --mock-latency S delays each reply.

docs.title: Prompt and harness optimizers
docs.text:
An optimizer evaluates many candidates of a program on many cases, and most candidates differ from their parent in one place. With Copula, a candidate pays only for the calls its edit changed, and the comparison of a child with its parent is made on the same samples wherever the two agree.

For that, Copula needs to know where each evaluation begins and ends. A whole optimizer process is one run, and inside one run the k-th identical request reads the k-th sample, so two candidates that make the same call inside one process would get different samples. Each evaluation of a candidate on a case is therefore a unit: a run of its own inside the process, with coordinates such as candidate and case.

docs.title: DSPy and GEPA, unchanged
docs.text:
Under copula run --exp, a DSPy program gets units without any change: the DSPy adapter makes each top-level module call a unit whose candidate is a hash of the module's state (instructions, demos, signatures) and whose case is a hash of the call's inputs. The seed of an optimizer is a replicate coordinate optimizer_seed.

$ copula run --exp gepa -- python gepa_math.py --out results/v1.json

This is the output of a cosmetic edit to such a program (DSPy 3 with GEPA, Qwen2.5-1.5B served by vLLM): 234 of its 238 calls were read from the first run.

copula: run r-d1938878157b4115  exp=gepa  dev: version v-116788f2fcb14d7f, slot 1  group g-f81577c06785524d543be1b3
copula: coordinates: {"annotation": ["out"]}
copula: new version (compared with earlier versions of gepa)
copula: attach: attached to http://127.0.0.1:32841/ (threads copy context; headers on httpx, httpx2, http.client)
copula: attach: GEPA adapter on: one decision scope per proposal, proposer role for reflection
copula: attach: DSPy response cache turned off (W11): it returned one stored sample for every repeat; repeated evaluations are now new samples, reused across runs by Copula
copula: attach: DSPy adapter on: units from module calls, candidates and seeds from optimizers, holdout evaluations
copula: attach: W5b: an Evaluate after compile scores 8 of 8 examples the optimizer used; those scores are optimistic
copula: run r-d1938878157b4115 done: 238 calls: 234 reused, 4 generated, 0 joined, 216 units

What the adapters do:

  • DSPy's response cache is turned off. It returns one stored response for every repeat of a request, so repeated evaluations of a candidate would all see one sample. Copula reuses samples across runs instead, and keeps repeats independent (note W11).
  • Holdout is inferred. A dspy.Evaluate after compile, outside it, on examples the optimizer was never given, is a holdout evaluation: it gets samples that no search evaluation read. An Evaluate on examples the optimizer used stays in the search phase, with warning W5b: its scores are optimistic.
  • GEPA proposals are decision scopes. Each proposal (evaluate the parent on a minibatch, reflect, evaluate the child) is one decision: on each case, the child reads the parent's slot when it can, so the acceptance test is paired.
  • Reflection calls carry the role proposer. --route proposer=RULE decides their group (Routes).

The few calls an edit regenerates without changing their request come from evaluation order: identical units (same candidate, same case) are numbered in the order they start, and a minibatch that holds one example twice can take them in another order (arrival_order).

docs.title: Your own optimizer loop
docs.text:
A hand-written loop marks its units with copula.run(**coordinates). Here three candidate system prompts are scored on three training questions, and the best one is evaluated on two test questions in the holdout phase:

optimize.py
import copula
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()
TRAIN = ["Why is the sky blue?", "What is a prime number?", "Who wrote Hamlet?"]
TEST = ["What is DNA?", "Why do leaves fall?"]
CANDIDATES = ["Answer in one sentence.", "Answer in one sentence. Be precise.",
              "Answer briefly and cite one fact."]


def solve(system, question):
    r = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct", temperature=0.7,
        messages=[{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": question}])
    return r.choices[0].message.content


def score(answer):
    return len(answer) % 7          # stands in for a real metric


best = None
for i, system in enumerate(CANDIDATES):
    total = 0
    for q in TRAIN:
        with copula.run(candidate=i, case=q):      # one unit per (candidate, case)
            total += score(solve(system, q))
    if best is None or total > best[0]:
        best = (total, system)

with copula.holdout():                             # final numbers on samples search never read
    for q in TEST:
        with copula.run(case=q):
            solve(best[1], q)
print("best:", best[1])

$ copula run --exp opt --mock -- python optimize.py
copula: run r-7bb1bf2e72f74072  exp=opt  dev: version v-929d10299905480b, slot 1  group g-7c415bbbf520985501803771
copula: served by embedded server (mock model)
copula: new version (compared with earlier versions of opt)
copula: attach: attached to http://127.0.0.1:45725/ (threads copy context; headers on httpx, httpx2, http.client)
best: Answer in one sentence.
copula: run r-7bb1bf2e72f74072 done: 11 calls: 0 reused, 11 generated, 0 joined, 11 units
copula:   11 generated: new request -- no earlier run of the experiment called this model
copula:   details: copula explain r-7bb1bf2e72f74072

Now replace the third candidate and run again:

CANDIDATES = [..., "Answer briefly and name your source."]

$ copula run --exp opt --mock -- python optimize.py
copula: run r-41771a4bf73c4b9e  exp=opt  dev: version v-2a09fbea2e744863, slot 1  group g-7c415bbbf520985501803771
copula: served by embedded server (mock model)
copula: new version (compared with earlier versions of opt)
copula: attach: attached to http://127.0.0.1:41315/ (threads copy context; headers on httpx, httpx2, http.client)
best: Answer in one sentence.
copula: run r-41771a4bf73c4b9e done: 11 calls: 8 reused, 3 generated, 0 joined, 11 units
copula:   3 generated: new request -- closest earlier request (run r-7bb1bf2e72f74072): messages[0] (system): '...briefly and cite one fact.' -> '...briefly and name your source.'
copula:   details: copula explain r-41771a4bf73c4b9e

The first two candidates read all their samples from the first run; only the new candidate's three calls were generated. The holdout evaluation is shared too when the same candidate wins: holdout units of different versions share with each other, as search units do, but never with the search phase.

copula.run blocks nest: a unit opened inside another merges its coordinates over the outer ones. The context follows the code into ThreadPoolExecutor workers and asyncio tasks, so units work in parallel evaluation loops.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
When a child candidate is accepted or rejected by comparing it with its parent on the same cases, the comparison is sharper if both read the same samples where their calls agree. Wrap the pair in copula.decision():

with copula.decision():
    parent_scores = [evaluate(parent, case) for case in minibatch]   # units inside
    child_scores = [evaluate(child, case) for case in minibatch]

Inside a decision, the units on one case read the samples of the decision's first unit on that case (its slot), unless this unit has already used that slot.

docs.title: Routes for roles
docs.text:
Calls made inside copula.role("proposer") (or with the header X-Copula-Role: proposer) carry a role, and --route ROLE=RULE chooses their group:

rule the calls of that role run (default) the group of the run or unit they are made in global one group per experiment, phase and role: every run shares them per:COORD one group per value of the run's coordinate COORD, e.g. per:seed fresh uncached: a new sample every time

For example, --route proposer=per:seed lets two runs with the same seed share their reflection calls, while different seeds propose independently. Routes apply within an experiment; a run without --exp ignores them. Calls routed global or per: are shared across slots, so they are not independent between reruns.

docs.title: One server for many runs
docs.text:
copula run serves its run itself when no server is running: an embedded server that lives as long as the command. The sample store of a project can be open in one process only, so for several commands at once (replicates, sweeps, a Slurm array, two terminals) start one copula server for the project. Every copula run in the project finds it and is served by it.

$ copula server &
copula: server http://127.0.0.1:42921 for /home/me/project (vllm http://gpu-node:8000/v1, engine seed per address)
{"event": "ready", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:42921", "pid": 2498623}

The server takes the model server options (--upstream, --model-dir, --mock, ...) and writes .copula/server.json, through which runs find it. It stops on Ctrl-C or SIGTERM and removes the file; a file left behind by a server that died on this host is removed by the next command. One server per project: a second copula server refuses to start.

agent.py
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()
for q in ["Why is the sky blue?", "Who wrote Hamlet?"]:
    r = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct", temperature=0.7,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": q}])
    print(r.choices[0].message.content)

With the server running (here started with --mock), runs name no model options:

$ copula run --exp demo --set rep=1 -- python agent.py
copula: run r-e6ea9df2ea1a4875  exp=demo  dev: version v-2c6ebe6a89704473, slot 1  group g-a174ef6155973219d0d1a48f
copula: served by server http://127.0.0.1:38687 (mock model)
copula: coordinates: {"replicate": ["rep"]}
copula: new version (compared with earlier versions of demo)
copula: attach: attached to http://127.0.0.1:38687/ (threads copy context; headers on httpx, httpx2, http.client)
mock:4ce416d39ab6bf39ff4c20bc
mock:4670b5a6cfb51fc28ed025df
copula: run r-e6ea9df2ea1a4875 done: 2 calls: 0 reused, 2 generated, 0 joined
copula:   2 generated: new request -- no earlier run of the experiment called this model
copula:   details: copula explain r-e6ea9df2ea1a4875

The model options belong to the server, and copula run refuses them rather than ignore them:

$ copula run --exp demo --model-dir /models/qwen -- python agent.py
copula run: the Copula server http://127.0.0.1:38687 decides the model server, so --model-dir cannot be set here: drop it, or stop the server

docs.title: Concurrent runs
docs.text:
Runs served by one server may run at the same time. When two of them need the same sample at the same moment (same group, same request, same occurrence), it is generated once: the second waits for it and reads it, and its summary counts it as joined.

$ for seed in 1 2 3 4; do copula run --exp sweep -- python agent.py --seed $seed & done; wait

Runs registered at the same moment see each other: two launches of one unchanged program take different slots, so they draw different samples.

docs.title: Slurm and other hosts
docs.text:
By default the server listens on 127.0.0.1 and serves runs on its own host. To serve launchers on other hosts, listen on a reachable address and give the launchers the URL and the server token:

$ copula server --listen 0.0.0.0:7000 --upstream http://gpu-node:8000/v1 &
$ export COPULA_SERVER_TOKEN=$(python -c 'import json; print(json.load(open(".copula/server.json"))["token"])')
$ sbatch --array=0-9 --export=ALL --wrap 'copula run --exp sweep --server http://login1:7000 -- python agent.py'
  • Each array task is a replicate: SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID becomes the coordinate slurm_array_task_id.
  • The launcher on the other host computes the content digests of the files that decide the version itself, so the project should be at the same path there (a shared file system). A file it cannot read counts as unchanged, which makes the run a rerun: new samples, never a wrong replay.
  • The token is a secret: with it, anyone who can reach the port can register runs and read stored samples. Traffic is plain HTTP, so listen on a trusted network only.

docs.title: What the server holds
docs.text: Everything lives in the project's .copula/ directory, private to its owner: the sample store, the registry of runs, the call log that copula explain reads, and server.json (Files and environment). The server is the only writer of the registry; copula explain and copula ls read it while the server runs.

docs.title: Why was this call generated?
docs.text: Every call Copula answers is either reused (read from the store), joined (another run was generating the same sample at that moment, and this one waited for it) or generated. For each generated call, Copula records why it could not be reused. The summary at the end of a run shows the main reasons with an example of each, and copula explain shows all of them.

docs.title: Look at a run
docs.text:
ask.py
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()
system = open("prompts/system.txt").read()
for q in ["Why is the sky blue?", "Who wrote Hamlet?"]:
    r = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct", temperature=0.7,
        messages=[{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": q}])
    print(r.choices[0].message.content)
