The run line gives the run's version, slot and group, and the run it is a rerun of. Each call line gives its sequence number in the call log, the run or unit, the node (actor:s is a sampled call to the default model), the outcome and the reason. --json prints the same as JSON lines for scripts: one object per run and unit, and with --calls one per call.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
When calls you expected to be reused were generated:

  1. Is the run in an experiment? Without --exp, a run shares nothing.
  2. Is it an unchanged rerun? Then it draws new samples by design (rerun). An edited program, or one with other compare coordinates, is a new version and shares.
  3. Do the coordinates differ? Runs with different replicate or case values, phases or experiments never share (replicate). Unknown names are replicates: look at the coordinates: line of the banner and class a name with --compare NAME or --annotation NAME if it should not separate runs.
  4. Did the request change? new_request shows the nearest earlier request and where it differs. Timestamps, random ids, unordered sets or unseeded shuffles in a prompt make every request new.
  5. Did the model change? A new checkpoint, server version or sampling table is a new model revision (model).

docs.title: Reasons
docs.text: Copula reports the first reason that applies. It checks uncached, after_error, new_request and model first. If an earlier run stored the request in this run's own group, the reason is more_repeats (or unexplained). Otherwise the groups differ, and it checks what keeps them apart: experiment, phase, granularity, replicate, case, seed, route, then the unit's ordinal (more_repeats or arrival_order), rerun and finally slot.

docs.title: uncached
docs.text: The call is not cached: its role is routed fresh (--route ROLE=fresh), so it is drawn anew every time. Fix: nothing to fix if that is the route you mean. (Requests that rely on provider-side state are refused rather than passed through.)

docs.title: after_error
docs.text: Earlier runs sent this request, but every earlier attempt failed (the upstream refused it or was unreachable), so there was no sample to reuse. Misconfiguration and transport errors are never stored, so the request is generated again once the upstream answers.

docs.title: new_request
docs.text:
No earlier run of the experiment sent this request to this model. The explanation names the closest earlier request and the first place where they differ:

3 generated: new request -- closest earlier request (run r-74437c2a66b94f2e): messages[0] (system): '...eply OK, or give a corrected answer.' -> '...eply OK, or explain the mistake.'

The path (messages[0], temperature, tools[1].function.description, ...) says which field changed. A call whose input contains the output of a call that was itself generated is a new request too: its prompt holds a new sample.

Fix: if the change is not one you made, look for volatile values in the prompt: the current date or time, request ids, set or dict iteration order, unseeded random. Make them stable, or keep them out of the request.

docs.title: model
docs.text: Earlier runs sent the same request to another revision of the model: other weights, another server version, another sampling table or other serving settings (Model identity). Samples are never served across revisions.

docs.title: more_repeats
docs.text: The request was sent more times in this run's group than earlier runs sent it: occurrence 4 when three are stored, say. The first three were reused, the rest generated. For units, it also covers a run with more identical units (same coordinates) than earlier runs had.

docs.title: rerun
docs.text: The program and every file it read are unchanged since an earlier run, so this run is a rerun: a new replicate, which takes a new slot and draws new samples. Fix: if you wanted the earlier outputs, you wanted a replay, which this version does not provide.

docs.title: arrival_order
docs.text: Units with equal coordinates are numbered in the order they start. This unit and the one that stored the sample have the same coordinates but other ordinals, because they started in another order: in a parallel evaluation, say, or when a batch holds one example twice. Each run still sees fresh, independent samples; they are only assigned differently. Fix: a coordinate that tells the units apart (case=...) makes the assignment stable.

docs.title: replicate
docs.text: Earlier runs sent the request with another value of a replicate coordinate (seed=1 here, seed=2 there, or unset). Replicates never share. Fix: if the name is not a replicate index, class it: --compare NAME or --annotation NAME.

docs.title: case
docs.text: Earlier runs sent the request for another case (a coordinate of the case class). Cases are kept apart.

docs.title: phase
docs.text: Earlier runs sent it in the other phase: search and holdout never share.

docs.title: seed
docs.text: Earlier runs sent it with another seed in the request body; each seed is its own sample stream.

docs.title: route
docs.text: Earlier runs sent it with another role, which --route places in another group.

docs.title: experiment
docs.text: Earlier runs of another experiment sent it. Experiments never share.

docs.title: granularity
docs.text: Earlier runs sent it from a whole process run and this run from a unit, or the other way around. A process run and a unit never share, so keep the unit structure of an experiment the same across its runs.

docs.title: slot
docs.text: Earlier runs stored it in another slot of the same version and coordinates, for example replicates launched at the same moment.

docs.title: unexplained
docs.text: The sample was stored in this run's group by a run that generated it at the same time, or the records needed to explain it are gone. Rare; not an error.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
src/copula/
  launcher.py      the copula command: run, server, explain, ls
  server.py        the Copula server: store, kernel manager, proxy, discovery
  proxy.py         the HTTP endpoint: model protocols, control API, units, retries
  protocols.py     Chat Completions, Responses and Anthropic Messages, to and from chat form
  registry.py      runs and units: versions, slots, groups, decisions, holdout checks
  coords.py        coordinate classes, recipes, command-line parsing
  attrs.py         how a request is classified (sampled, greedy, uncached)
  upstream.py      model servers: vLLM, SGLang, APIs; sampling tables, identity, engine seeds
  calls.py         the call log and the reasons of copula explain
  client.py        copula.run, holdout, decision, role, headers, chat
  _attach.py       copula.attach: threads, HTTP headers, adapters
  adapters/        DSPy and GEPA
  _shim/           the start-up hook (Python read tracing) and the Node read recorder
  testing.py       the scripted mock model
  kernel/          the paper's kernel: SDK, cache manager, store, keys (byte for byte)
tests/             unit and end-to-end tests; tests/kernel holds the kernel's own tests
docs/              this documentation (MkDocs)
tools/             import_kernel.py

docs.title: The kernel
docs.text:
copula.kernel is a byte-for-byte copy of the kernel the paper evaluated. kernel/PROVENANCE.json records the sha256 of every file, and tests/test_provenance.py fails if any file differs. Changes to sharing semantics belong in the layers around the kernel. To bring in a new frozen kernel:

python tools/import_kernel.py SRC_DIR --tests TESTS_DIR

It copies the kernel files, rewrites PROVENANCE.json, and ports the kernel's tests into tests/kernel (imports rewritten, static-graph tests skipped).

The comments of the kernel and of tests/kernel call it by its research name, evalrt, and cite design notes of the research repository (reports/...), which are not published. The research code's static-graph executor stays behind, so the Session methods for static graphs (program, graph_bound, execute, execute_sync, forecast) raise ImportError in this package.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
PYTHONPATH=src:. python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

The suite needs only the standard library and runs against the mock model. Tests that need openai, anthropic, DSPy or Node are skipped when they are missing; COPULA_DSPY_PYTHON and COPULA_ANTHROPIC_PYTHON name interpreters that have them.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The pages are Markdown in docs/, built with MkDocs and the Material theme:

pip install '.[docs]'   # MkDocs 1.6 and Material 9, pinned in pyproject.toml
mkdocs serve            # http://127.0.0.1:8000
mkdocs build --strict   # what CI runs

tests/test_docs.py keeps the pages true:

  • Each page is run as a script in a fresh project: a code block with a title="FILE" writes that file, and each $ command of a console block is run, its output compared with the lines below it. Ids that change from run to run (runs, versions, groups, ports, mock replies) are compared by pattern. HTML comments <!-- docs-test: ... --> add hidden steps (run, bg, wait) or mark the next block (skip for a real model server, fails for a command that must fail).
  • The command-line reference must list exactly the parser's options, the coordinate tables must match coords.py, every copula explain reason must have a section, every page must be in the navigation, and every link must resolve.

After a change to the output, regenerate the transcripts and review the diff:

COPULA_DOCS_UPDATE=1 PYTHONPATH=src:. python -m unittest tests.test_docs

The examples need the openai package (COPULA_DOCS_PYTHON names an interpreter that has it).

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
copula [--version] {run, server, explain, ls} ...

copula --version prints the version; copula COMMAND --help lists a command's options. python -m copula is the same command.

docs.title: copula run
docs.text:
copula run [options] [model server options] -- COMMAND [ARGS...]

Runs COMMAND as one run of the project and serves its model calls: through the project's copula server when one is running (found in .copula/server.json), through the server named by --server, or else through a server embedded in this command. Exits with the command's status.

option default meaning --exp NAME none the experiment. Runs of one experiment share samples; a run without one shares nothing. With --exp, the files the program reads decide its version, and Python children are attached --project DIR . the project: where .copula/ lives, and the only files that count for versions --recipe NAME dev default classes for coordinate names of a kind of workload: dev, eval, optimize, ab, sweep, tts, sdg, rl (recipes) --phase PHASE search search or holdout; the phases never share (phases) --set K=V a coordinate of the run (repeatable) --compare NAME class coordinate NAME as compare: runs that differ in it share (repeatable) --replicate NAME class it as replicate: runs that differ in it never share --case NAME class it as case: runs that differ in it never share --annotation NAME class it as annotation: recorded, ignored --route ROLE=RULE run the group of calls made with role ROLE: run, global, fresh or per:COORD (routes) --track GLOB project files whose content belongs to the version, for programs Copula does not trace (repeatable; ** allowed) --no-attach do not attach Python children: no adapters, no unit context --server URL the URL of a copula server on another host; the token comes from $COPULA_SERVER_TOKEN

The model server options below apply when this command serves the run itself. With a live server they belong to the server, and copula run refuses them.

The run prints its placement before the command starts and a summary when it ends, on stderr (Messages).

docs.title: copula server
docs.text:
copula server [--listen HOST[:PORT]] [model server options]

Serves every run of the project from one process until Ctrl-C or SIGTERM (One server for many runs). Writes .copula/server.json, prints a line on stderr and one JSON line {"event": "ready", "url": ..., "pid": ...} on stdout when it is ready. Refuses to start if a server already runs for the project.

option default meaning --project DIR . the project --listen HOST[:PORT] 127.0.0.1, any free port the address to serve on; 0.0.0.0:PORT serves other hosts

docs.title: Model server options
docs.text:
Options of copula run (embedded server) and copula server (Connect a model server).

option default meaning --upstream URL $OPENAI_BASE_URL the OpenAI-compatible model server to forward to --served-model NAME the first listed the default model of the upstream; needed when it lists no models --model-dir DIR the files of the default model: they establish its identity and give its sampling defaults --defaults JSON a pinned sampling table for the default model, as JSON or @FILE, naming all nine sampling parameters; overrides generation_config.json --identity-extra JSON serving settings that change outputs (dtype, quantisation), as JSON or @FILE; vLLM and SGLang only --engine-seed MODE auto address: an engine seed per sample address; off: none; auto: address for vLLM, off otherwise --api-key-env VAR OPENAI_API_KEY the variable holding the upstream's key --model NAME[=SERVED] a client-side model name for a served model (repeatable); '*' takes any name --max-tokens N 1024 max_tokens of requests that set none --max-attempts N 6 attempts of a generation that fails with a transport error, a timeout, 5xx, 408, 409, 429 or 401/403/404/405/407 --backoff S 0.5 base of the exponential retry backoff, seconds --timeout S 900 upstream request timeout, seconds --workers N 64 upstream requests in flight --inflight N 64 generations in flight per model --wait-ready S 0 wait up to S seconds for the upstream to answer --keepalive S 15 seconds between keep-alives of a buffered stream --no-identity treat every model's identity as not established: greedy calls are cached per group --mock serve the mock model instead of an upstream --mock-script FILE.py:FUNC script the mock's replies (MODULE:FUNC works too); implies --mock --mock-nonce TEXT copula-mock another nonce gives the mock other replies --mock-latency S 0 the mock's delay per reply, seconds --manager SOCKET serve from a running kernel manager instead (python -m copula.kernel.manager); its model is named actor unless --model names it, and its identity counts as established --trace write the kernel's trace to .copula/trace.jsonl

docs.title: copula explain
docs.text:
copula explain [RUN] [--calls] [--json]

How a run was placed (experiment, phase, version, slot, group, coordinates, the run it reruns) and why each of its calls was generated (Why was this call generated?).

option default meaning RUN last a run id, a unique prefix of one, a unit id (its process run is shown), last or last~N (the N-th run before the latest) --project DIR . the project --calls one line per call --json JSON lines: one object per run and unit; with --calls, one per call too

docs.title: copula ls
docs.text:
copula ls [--exp NAME]

Lists the runs and units of the project, oldest first: id, experiment, phase, kind (process run or unit), status of process runs (running, done, or unknown when the command failed or its launcher died), version, slot and group.

option default meaning --project DIR . the project --exp NAME all only the runs of this experiment

docs.title: Coordinate names and recipes
docs.text: The class of a coordinate name decides what it does to sharing (Runs, coordinates and versions). This page lists the names Copula knows. Every other name is a replicate.

docs.title: Built-in names
docs.text:
Names are compared after normalisation: lower case, leading dashes removed, - read as _.

class names compare variant, version, candidate, config, arm, method, budget, prompt replicate seed, trial, rep, repeat, replicate, attempt, epoch, rollout, shard, chunk, fold, slurm_array_task_id, and every name not listed on this page case case, example, sample_id, doc_id, task_id, instance, problem annotation iteration, metric_key, workflow_name, group_id, trace_id, session_id, thread_id, run_name, name, o, out, outdir, output, output_dir, log_dir, logdir, save_dir, savedir

Also annotations: every name of the form o, out, output, log, logs, save or ckpt followed by dir, path, file or prefix, with or without _ (output_path, log_file, ckptdir, ...).

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text:
--recipe NAME adds names to these defaults for a kind of workload. A recipe never turns an unknown name into anything but a replicate except through its own list.

recipe adds dev nothing: the defaults above (the default recipe) eval compare: task, task_identifier, model_config, solver; case: sample, test, test_idx optimize annotation: parent tts compare: n, beam_width, num_beams ab nothing yet sweep nothing yet sdg nothing yet rl nothing yet

ab, sweep, sdg and rl are accepted and recorded with the run; in this version they class names like dev. Overrides (--compare, --replicate, --case, --annotation) take precedence over the recipe.

docs.title: Where coordinates come from
docs.text:
source example gives --name value, --name=value python agent.py --variant strict variant=strict -x value python agent.py -o out/v2 o=out/v2 (an annotation) Hydra-style overrides python train.py lr=3e-4 +model.size=7b lr=3e-4, model.size=7b --set copula run --set rep=2 -- ... rep=2 Slurm SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID=3 slurm_array_task_id=3 copula.run(...) copula.run(candidate=i, case=q) unit coordinates X-Copula-Coords X-Copula-Coords: case=17;arm=b unit coordinates DSPy adapter candidate, case, optimizer_seed (a replicate)

Positional words give no coordinate, and a lone -- ends the options. A flag followed by a word that is not an option takes it as its value (python -u agent.py gives u=agent.py); a flag followed by another option, or last on the line, gives none. A word after a flag that looks like an override (--fast lr=3e-4) is an override, not the flag's value. Values are compared as strings.

docs.title: The .copula/ directory
docs.text:
Copula keeps everything of a project in .copula/ in the project directory, created on the first run with permissions 0700. Deleting it forgets every sample and run of the project.

path content entries.db the sample store (SQLite), with the secret that engine seeds are derived with registry.db runs and units: versions, slots, groups, coordinates, read sets; the secret behind run tokens; the Responses objects Copula issued calls.db the call log: one row per answered call and each distinct request body, read by copula explain server.json the live server: URL, host, pid, token and upstream (0600; removed when the server stops) runs/<run>/reads.<pid> the files each process of a run read and wrote pylib/ a link to the copula package, put on the children's PYTHONPATH m.sock the kernel manager's socket while a server runs (in a temporary directory if the path is too long) trace.jsonl the kernel trace, with --trace

The call log is diagnostic only: nothing reads it to decide what a request returns.

docs.title: Variables set for the command
docs.text:
copula run sets these in the command's environment:

variable value OPENAI_BASE_URL, OPENAI_API_BASE, LLM_BASE_URL, COPULA_URL the run's URL, http://HOST:PORT/r/TOKEN/v1 ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_API_BASE the run's URL without /v1 OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY copula, when not set already (the key is not used) COPULA_RUN the run id COPULA_EXP the experiment, or empty COPULA_MODEL the model server's default model COPULA_PROJECT the project directory COPULA_READS_FILE where Python and Node children record the files they read COPULA_ATTACH 1 with --exp (and without --no-attach): Python children attach PYTHONPATH Copula's start-up hook and .copula/pylib, before the existing value NODE_OPTIONS --require of Copula's read recorder, after the existing value (with --exp)

COPULA_SERVER_TOKEN is removed from the command's environment.

docs.title: Variables Copula reads
docs.text: variable used by meaning OPENAI_BASE_URL copula run, copula server the upstream, unless --upstream OPENAI_API_KEY copula run, copula server the upstream's key (or the variable --api-key-env names) COPULA_SERVER_TOKEN copula run --server the token of a server on another host SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID copula run becomes the coordinate slurm_array_task_id COPULA_QUIET attached Python children silences the copula: attach: lines HF_HUB_CACHE, HF_HOME the server where to look for a model's Hugging Face snapshot

docs.title: HTTP interface
docs.text: A Copula server speaks the model protocols on one port and a small control API next to them. copula run uses both; a program needs only the model endpoints, which its base URL already points to.

docs.title: Model endpoints
docs.text:
POST <base>/r/<token>/v1/chat/completions     OpenAI Chat Completions
POST <base>/r/<token>/v1/responses            OpenAI Responses
GET  <base>/r/<token>/v1/responses/<id>       a response this server issued
POST <base>/r/<token>/v1/messages             Anthropic Messages
GET  <base>/r/<token>/v1/models               the models served

<token> names the run and proves that the caller may use it. The same paths without /r/<token> work when the request carries the token in the header X-Copula-Run: <token>. Once a run has ended its token is no longer accepted (HTTP 401), because a late attempt could re-read samples its client already received.

docs.title: Request headers
docs.text:
All optional; values are percent-encoded.

header meaning X-Copula-Coords: k=v;k=v the request belongs to a unit of the run with these coordinates X-Copula-Unit: N the unit's ordinal among units with the same coordinates (default 1) X-Copula-Phase: holdout a holdout unit; without coordinates, the process run's one holdout unit, shared by every such request X-Copula-Phase-Source: inferred the phase is a guess (by an adapter): on a case overlap, fall back to the search phase instead of refusing X-Copula-Decision: ID the unit belongs to a decision scope X-Copula-Role: NAME the call has a role, placed by the run's routes x-stainless-retry-count, Idempotency-Key a client retry: re-read the occurrence whose response was lost, instead of taking the next one

A retry re-reads an occurrence of the same request in the same run whose response was never delivered and whose client connection is gone, within 600 s; an Idempotency-Key matches only a key the run has sent before. copula.headers() builds the X-Copula-* headers for the current Python context (Python API).

docs.title: Response headers
docs.text:
header meaning x-copula-run the run or unit the call belonged to x-copula-group its group x-copula-rule how the run was placed, how the call was classified, and the protocol x-copula-status per sample: generated, hit (stored by another run), own (stored earlier by this run), waited (joined a generation in flight). The run summary counts hit and own as reused and waited as joined x-copula-rank per sample: its occurrence in the group, or - for a greedy call

A streamed response carries the status and rank as a final SSE comment (: x-copula-status generated; x-copula-rank 1). Streams are buffered: keep-alive comments (an Anthropic ping event for Messages) until the sample is ready, then the protocol's events.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Errors come in the protocol's own error format. A streamed request that was admitted gets HTTP 200 at once, so an error of its generation arrives as a stream event; a request refused before that gets an ordinary error reply. Error replies carry x-should-retry: false, so the openai SDK does not retry them.

status when 400 invalid_call, invalid_request a malformed request, or a field Copula refuses (invalid_request from the Responses and Anthropic adapters) 400 model_error the model server rejected the request itself; stored as the sample's result 401 no_run no valid run token, or the run has ended 404 model_not_found a model this server does not serve 404 not_found no such endpoint, or a response id this server did not issue 405 the wrong method for the endpoint 409 holdout_overlap a holdout unit for a case the search phase used 410 run_ended the run ended while the request was being admitted 500 internal a bug in Copula 502 the model server failed after --max-attempts attempts; nothing was stored 503 closing the server is shutting down

Responses objects that Copula issued, and the chains behind them, are kept in the project's registry; GET /v1/responses/ID returns them to any valid run token of the project.

docs.title: Control API
docs.text:
The control endpoints need the server token (Authorization: Bearer <token>, from .copula/server.json). They are how copula run registers runs with a live server, locally or with --server.

GET  <base>/copula/v1/health              the server's upstream, models and state
POST <base>/copula/v1/paths               {experiment, coords, ...} -> {paths}: the files whose
                                          digests decide a new run's version
POST <base>/copula/v1/runs                {experiment, recipe, phase, coords, overrides, routes,
                                          digests, owner} -> {run, url}: register a process run
POST <base>/copula/v1/runs/<run>/end      {reads, ok} -> {stats, counts, units, notes, why}: end it

A run registered through the control API is served until it is ended; the launcher ends it when its command exits.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
copula run writes its messages to stderr, each line starting with copula:. This page explains them in the order they appear.

Some messages carry a code, so that they can be searched for and named in bug reports:

code condition O1 a run without an experiment gets a fresh group V2 a seed in the request selects its own sample stream W1 a run of an experiment reused every sample W5a a holdout unit's case was used in the search phase (refused) W5b an evaluation after optimisation scores examples the optimizer used W8 a framework cache could not be turned off W11 a framework cache was turned off W12 a model's identity is not established: greedy calls are cached per group

docs.title: Placement
docs.text:
copula: run r-5e77ae7d7cf040a3  exp=demo  dev: version v-dcb9767f264042f9, slot 1  group g-0e5d5aee9cfa7a183956942b

The run id, the experiment (- for none), the recipe, and where the run was placed: its version, slot and group (How Copula works). Without --exp: no experiment: fresh group (O1).

docs.title: served by
docs.text: served by embedded server (...) when this command serves the run itself, served by server URL (...) when a copula server does. In parentheses: the upstream's kind and URL, and engine seed per address when vLLM gets per-sample engine seeds.

docs.title: Upstream notes
docs.text: note meaning sampling defaults: MODEL generation_config the pinned sampling table comes from the model's generation_config.json sampling defaults: MODEL --defaults it comes from --defaults sampling defaults: MODEL neutral (...) no generation_config.json found (no model files, or none among them): neutral values. Native vLLM would apply the model's generation_config.json if it has one; pass --model-dir identity of MODEL not established (...) (W12) greedy calls to it are cached per group, not globally; --model-dir establishes it API upstream: temperature and top_p are always sent ... an API upstream gets OpenAI's defaults when the client sets none; pass --defaults for another provider an API upstream takes no engine seed --engine-seed address was given for an API upstream and is ignored

docs.title: coordinates:
docs.text: The coordinate names of the run by class, e.g. {"compare": ["variant"], "replicate": ["seed"]}. Look here when runs you expected to share did not: an unknown name is a replicate.

docs.title: Version
docs.text: line meaning new version (compared with earlier versions of EXP) the program, its files or its compare values changed: it shares with earlier versions unchanged since run R: a rerun (new slot, new samples) nothing changed: a new replicate unchanged since run R; first run of this version with these replicate or case values (new group, new samples) nothing changed in the program, but the replicate or case values are new run R of this experiment is still running, so its files are not known yet: counted as unchanged ... a rerun of a run that has not finished run R failed, so the files it read are unknown: counted as unchanged ... a rerun of a failed run holdout phase: new group space; ... --phase holdout: the run's groups are apart from the search phase's; whether its cases overlap the search phase is checked for units only

docs.title: Attach
docs.text:
Lines from Python children, starting with copula: attach:; COPULA_QUIET=1 silences them.

line meaning attached to URL (...) the process is attached to its run DSPy adapter on: ..., GEPA adapter on: ... an adapter was installed when the framework was imported DSPy response cache turned off (W11): ... DSPy's cache would have answered repeats from one sample; Copula reuses samples instead could not turn off the DSPy cache (W8): ... repeats may be collapsed by DSPy before they reach Copula W5b: an Evaluate after compile scores N of M examples the optimizer used; those scores are optimistic an evaluation on selection data, left in the search phase adapter NAME failed for ... the adapter could not be installed; the program runs without it

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
copula: run r-5e77ae7d7cf040a3 done: 6 calls: 3 reused, 3 generated, 0 joined

Calls by outcome: reused (read from the store), generated, joined (waited for a generation in flight), and, when there are any, failed calls and the number of units. The outcomes count samples, so a request with n=3 counts three times; copula explain counts requests.

docs.title: N generated: REASON -- EXAMPLE
docs.text: Up to three reasons why calls were generated, with one example each (Why was this call generated?).

docs.title: note (Nx): ...
docs.text:
Notes about the run's requests, with their count:

note meaning seed S selects its own sample stream (V2); repeats inside one run are numbered, not identical identical seeded requests inside one run get different samples of the seed's stream (Seeds) greedy, but no established upstream identity: cached per group (W12) greedy calls were treated like sampled ones retry re-read an undelivered occurrence a client retry read the sample whose response it had lost

docs.title: W1
docs.text:
copula:   W1: every sample was read from earlier runs; if you wanted new samples, this run is a replicate (--set rep=2)

A run of an experiment generated nothing: everything was reused. That is what a cosmetic edit should do; if you meant to draw new samples, run a replicate.

docs.title: Failed command
docs.text: the command failed: the files it read are recorded as unknown for versioning means the command exited non-zero: its read set is not recorded, and the next run is counted as a rerun of it.

docs.title: details: copula explain RUN
docs.text: Shown when calls were generated: the command that explains them.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text: import copula needs only the standard library. A program run under copula run needs none of this: it is for programs that want to describe their structure more precisely than Copula infers it.

docs.title: Contexts
docs.text: The contexts below travel with the code: into nested calls, asyncio tasks and, once the process is attached, ThreadPoolExecutor workers. They reach Copula as X-Copula-* headers on the requests made inside them (HTTP interface). Attaching happens automatically under copula run --exp; without it, pass copula.headers() to your client yourself.

docs.title: copula.run(**coordinates)
docs.text:
with copula.run(candidate=cand_id, case=example_id):
    agent(example)

A unit: the calls made inside belong to a run of their own, with these coordinates merged over the enclosing ones. The k-th unit with the same coordinates in one process is a new unit (ordinal k), so it reads new samples. copula.run() without coordinates opens no unit. See Runs, coordinates and versions.

docs.title: copula.holdout()
docs.text:
with copula.holdout():
    for example in test_set:
        with copula.run(case=example["id"]):
            evaluate(best, example)

Units opened inside are in the holdout phase, which has groups of its own: its sampled calls share nothing with the search phase. A holdout unit whose case the search phase used is refused (HTTP 409). Calls made inside holdout() but outside any copula.run all belong to one holdout unit of the process.

docs.title: copula.decision(name=None)
docs.text:
with copula.decision():
    parent_score = evaluate(parent, minibatch)
    child_score = evaluate(child, minibatch)

A decision scope: a unit inside it reads the slot of the scope's first unit on the same case (unless it has used that slot already), so a parent and a child compared in one decision see the same samples where their calls agree. Without a name, each scope gets a new id.

docs.title: copula.role(name)
docs.text:
with copula.role("proposer"):
    new_prompt = reflect(traces)

Calls made inside carry the role, which copula run --route ROLE=RULE places (Routes).

docs.title: copula.headers(role=None)
docs.text:
The X-Copula-* headers of the current context, as a dict, for a client that attach() does not cover:

requests.post(url, json=body, headers={**copula.headers(), "Authorization": "Bearer x"})

docs.title: copula.chat(messages, model=None, **params)
docs.text: A chat completion through the run's Copula endpoint with the standard library alone. Returns the response as a dict, with the x-copula-* response headers under "_copula". model defaults to $COPULA_MODEL; other keyword arguments are request fields (temperature=0.7). Also takes base_url, role, timeout (600 s) and extra_headers.

docs.title: copula.attach(exp=None, url=None)
docs.text: Attaches the process to its run: copies the context into ThreadPoolExecutor workers, adds the headers to requests sent to Copula through httpx and http.client (urllib, urllib3, requests), and installs the framework adapters when DSPy or GEPA is imported. It is idempotent, and copula run --exp calls it before the program starts. url defaults to $COPULA_URL, which copula run sets; without a URL it raises RuntimeError. exp, if given, must equal the launcher's --exp.

docs.title: The kernel API
docs.text:
copula.Session is the interface of the paper's kernel: runs, groups and registered nodes, with no launcher, registry or inference. The program declares everything itself: each node's randomness and caching, and the group each run belongs to. It talks to a kernel manager, the process that owns the sample store.

$ python -m copula.kernel.manager --store kernel/store.db --socket kernel/m.sock --mock demo &
kernel_demo.py
from copula import Session

s = Session.connect_sync("kernel/m.sock")
s.register_llm("draft", cache=True, randomness="stochastic", pin={"temperature": 0.7})
s.register_llm("judge", cache=True, randomness="deterministic", pin={"temperature": 0.0})
dev = s.group("dev")


def agent(question):
    draft = s.chat_sync("draft", [{"role": "user", "content": question}])
    text = draft.choices[0].message.content
    verdict = s.chat_sync("judge", [{"role": "user", "content": "Is this right? " + text}])
    return text, verdict.choices[0].message.content


with s.run_sync(dev):           # a run in group "dev"
    print(agent("Why is the sky blue?"))
with s.run_sync(dev):           # another run of the group: its k-th call reads sample k
    print(agent("Why is the sky blue?"))
with s.run_sync(s.group()):     # a fresh group: new samples
    print(agent("Why is the sky blue?"))
s.close()

A cached node declares randomness, and a deterministic one must pin greedy decoding @s.tool(name=None, version=1, *, cache, randomness=None) a tool node; a cached stochastic tool takes an rng argument seeded from its address s.group(name=None) a named group (the same name is the same pool), or a fresh one with s.run_sync(group):, async with s.run(group): a run in the group; run_id= resumes a run, re-reading its samples in order s.chat_sync(model, messages, **params), await s.chat(...) a call of a registered node inside a run s.wrap(client) routes an openai client's chat completions through the session with s.intercept(): inside the block, routes every openai client in the process (those a framework creates too): a request whose model is a node registered here goes through the session, any other request goes out unchanged s.close(), await s.aclose() closes the session

copula.Group, copula.Run, copula.Namespace (the response objects) and copula.SDKError are exported too. copula.kernel holds the full kernel, byte for byte the code the paper evaluated (Development).
